writeup: Astronomers have identified a previously unknown eclipsing binary star system called TIC 70762350, where two stars orbit each other every 3.79 days. When the primary star passes in front of its companion, the system dims by 7.15 percent - a dip detected with high confidence by automated surveys. Interestingly, the secondary eclipse was not observed, suggesting the companion star may be significantly smaller or dimmer than the primary. The discovery passed rigorous vetting procedures, including pixel-level analysis and checks against existing catalogs of known variable stars, confirming this is a genuinely new find. This candidate represents the kind of stellar system that helps astronomers understand binary star properties and their orbital dynamics.
